result.summary: The pedestrian environment is centered around a transit hub with an elevated rail station and bus terminal, providing essential infrastructure like sidewalks and marked crossings. However, the large concrete pillars supporting the rail line create significant blind spots, and the lack of visible pedestrian signals at such a busy location is a safety concern.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large concrete pillars supporting the elevated rail line block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left of the image

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible at this complex intersection, which may lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear guidance on crossing phases.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the crossing to reduce crossing distance and improve the visibility of pedestrians to drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing transverse markings to high-visibility continental or ladder patterns to increase driver awareness.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and signalized pedestrian controls, providing a basic level of safety. However, the wide roadway with multiple travel lanes and a lack of physical buffers or refuge islands increases pedestrian exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lanes with no trees or physical barriers to separate pedestrians from moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the sidewalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Plant trees along the sidewalk to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, marked crosswalks, and signalization. However, the wide roadway and lack of physical buffers or refuge islands increase pedestrian exposure in an environment that appears designed primarily for vehicle throughput.

hazards.name: Wide Intersection Geometry
hazards.description: The wide, open nature of the intersection increases pedestrian exposure time and may encourage higher vehicle turning speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection where the red car is located

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or vertical element (like trees or bollards) between the sidewalk and the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk area on the left and far side of the intersection

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and reduce vehicle turning speeds.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing transverse markings to high-visibility continental-style markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical buffer for pedestrians and help naturally calm traffic speeds.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by an intersection located beneath an elevated rail structure, which creates significant visual obstructions via large support pillars. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the crosswalk markings are severely faded and dedicated pedestrian signals are not clearly visible.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk lines are heavily worn, making the pedestrian crossing area less visible to approaching motorists.

hazards.description: Large concrete pillars supporting the elevated rail structure block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
